faqs.question: What's the difference between SEO and MEO?
faqs.answer: SEO focuses on ranking in Google's web search results. MEO (Map Engine Optimization) focuses on ranking in Google Maps and the local 3-pack. For businesses with physical locations, MEO often delivers faster, higher-intent traffic.

faqs.question: How long until I see results from MEO?
faqs.answer: Timing varies by market, competition, profile history, customer activity, and platform changes. We establish the agreed foundation and measurement; we do not promise a specific ranking or date.

faqs.question: Do I need to respond to every review?
faqs.answer: We handle review monitoring and response templates. Responding to reviews — especially negative ones — is one of the highest-impact MEO activities. We'll draft responses and keep your profile active.

faqs.question: Can you help if I have multiple locations?
faqs.answer: Yes, when multiple locations are included in the signed Japan Entry scope. Each eligible Google Business Profile is handled with location-specific setup, content, measurement, and review-response responsibilities.

items.q: What exactly does the Japan Entry package cost?

items.q: When do the campaign months begin?

items.q: Which launch track is right for us?
items.a: Japan Digital Launch is for SaaS, AI, DevTools, education, and digital products; Japan Web3 Launch is for infrastructure, security, data, and API businesses; Japan Commerce Launch is for furniture, design, hobby, and premium cross-border commerce. All tracks share the same evidence-first market review, Japanese buyer path, workspace, QA, and handover. The Setup SOW records the track-specific acceptance checks.

items.q: How is setup different from managed operation?
items.a: Setup is a fixed milestone queue—Opportunity Analysis, Localization Strategy, Web Build, Payments, Social Media Setup, Initial Creative, QA, and Launch. Managed operation is a separate request queue after the applicable commencement date: requests are queued, one primary request is Active at a time, standard requests normally start within 48 business hours after inputs are ready, and material changes require a written Change Request.

items.q: What is included in the fixed setup?
items.a: The standard setup envelope covers Japan Opportunity analysis, a Japanese landing page plus an agreed core-page set (normally up to eight to ten pages and 15,000–20,000 source words), payment setup coordination, up to two Social Media channels, launch creative, a Notion or Trello workspace, regulatory-readiness coordination, launch management, and handover. The signed scope is the final source of truth.

items.q: What is not included?
items.a: Legal, tax, banking, licensing, certification, provider approval, advertising, creator, software, hosting, payment-processing, inventory, logistics, fulfilment, specialist, and other third-party costs are separate unless expressly added in writing. Large custom development, full website rebuilds, unbounded content or Social Media work, customer support, sales representation, and work outside the agreed launch scope are also separate.

items.q: What does the 14-business-day delivery guarantee cover?
items.a: The Start Date is recorded after written scope acceptance, cleared payment, complete source materials, required access, and one empowered approver. If the agreed fixed setup is not delivered within 14 business days, 100% of the $12,000 setup fee is refunded. Client-requested changes or holds pause the clock; sales outcomes are not guaranteed.

items.q: Who is the package designed for?
items.a: It is designed for established SMBs in Europe, North America, and Australia that can make a fast owner-led or executive decision. Sector and headcount are less important than decision speed, a real offer, and the ability to supply launch inputs.

items.q: Do we need a Japanese entity, bank account, or Japanese-speaking employee?
items.a: Not for every launch. The required structure depends on what you sell and how payment, fulfilment, support, and regulated obligations apply. We coordinate the launch path but do not replace legal, tax, banking, or licensed professional advice.

items.q: Can we cancel the ongoing service?
items.a: The setup engagement remains governed by the agreed scope. The first 10 selected launch partners receive months 1–6 at $0/month, followed by the standard $2,000/month managed-operation fee from month 7 onward under the signed terms; fees already earned and third-party commitments are not reversed.

items.q: What happens after we apply?
items.a: We review fit, authority, timeline, source context, and launch constraints. A submitted application is not acceptance of an engagement. If the package fits, we confirm scope, dependencies, terms, and the start date before work begins.

items.q: Which documents govern the engagement?
items.a: The public site is an overview, not the contract. Before kickoff, the agreed record may include master service terms, a Setup SOW, an Order Form and service schedule/SLA, plus a DPA, NDA, or payment addendum when needed. The written scope and signed terms—not a chat message—control the engagement.

items.q: How do you handle acceptance and change requests?
items.a: The Setup SOW records the deliverables, dependencies, approver, acceptance criteria, review window, and change-control path. A request that changes the accepted direction, adds a new deliverable, or depends on new access is logged as a Change Request and scheduled or priced separately in writing.

items.q: What must be ready before kickoff?
items.a: Prepare the current offer, brand and product source material, required account access, a preferred launch date, and one empowered approver. We also need to know which claims, payment flows, fulfilment steps, or regulated features require specialist review.

items.q: What happens during the first five business days?
items.a: We confirm the first Japanese offer, buyer path, ownership, inputs, acceptance criteria, and dependencies. Any blocker that could change the target is recorded before implementation proceeds.

items.q: How can we see progress after kickoff?
items.a: After written scope acceptance, we create a dedicated client workspace—normally Notion, or Trello if your team prefers. It shows the agreed tasks, owners, status, blockers, approvals, deliverables, request intake, files, and next action. During the included operation, the standard envelope is up to four pages or 5,000 words per month, one active creative request at a time, up to two Social Media channels, and a 48-business-hour start commitment for standard requests. These are planning boundaries, not simultaneous maximum-output guarantees.

items.q: Can you support B2B and non-ecommerce offers?
items.a: Yes. The buyer path may end in an inquiry, qualification, booking, proposal, or eligible payment route. The scope is shaped around the offer and the decision a Japanese buyer needs to make, not around a fixed ecommerce template.

items.q: How do you use public market data?
items.a: Public rank, crawl, sitemap, schema, and registry signals can show visibility and market alignment. Every material output is labelled Observed, Modeled, or Hypothesis and includes the source, capture date, confidence boundary, and next verification action. Public signals cannot prove actual monthly visits, country traffic share, or revenue; those remain unknown unless first-party or authorized data is provided.

items.q: What if the package is not the right fit?
items.a: The application is a fit review, not an obligation to proceed. If the decision authority, source material, timing, offer, or dependencies do not match the fixed scope, we identify that before accepting the engagement.

items.q: What do you mean by a guarantee?
items.a: We guarantee the agreed delivery process, scope, acceptance checks, and documented handover—not a ranking, traffic level, conversion rate, or revenue outcome. If a dependency is outside our control, it is recorded before kickoff rather than hidden behind a promise.

items.q: Are the Works examples real client case studies?
items.a: The Works page separates inspectable delivery dossiers from authorized client outcome studies. We show the buyer path, implementation evidence, acceptance checks, and unknowns; we do not present invented client names, revenue, or conversion results. A first-party case study is added only with permission and source data.

items.q: How does the AI assistant use our information?
items.a: The public assistant retrieves approved site and editorial context, then uses Gemini or the configured Dify app when available. It must not invent commercial terms. Sensitive account details, legal advice, and final scope stay in the human-reviewed application and written agreement.

items.q: What happens if a provider or regulator delays launch?
items.a: We surface the dependency, identify the affected route, and record an alternative inquiry or launch path where one is eligible. Provider approval, formal legal opinions, licences, banking, tax, and fulfilment remain external decisions and can move the target date.

queues.managedLabel: Managed Request Queue · included operating period
managed: Requests are submitted in the private client workspace with an owner, priority, context, and requested decision.

New standard requests are acknowledged within one business day and normally start within 48 business hours after required inputs are ready.

evidence.title: A model is useful only when its boundary is visible.
evidence.desc: Signal Check, market reports, and opportunity views separate what was observed from what was modelled and what still needs testing. No private traffic, country share, conversion, or revenue is presented as a fact without authorized first-party data.

labels.name: Observed
labels.body: A dated public or authorized first-party signal with a source URL, capture record, and confidence boundary.

labels.name: Modeled
labels.body: A range calculated from stated assumptions, retrieval date, formula, low/base/high cases, and a clear disclaimer.

labels.name: Hypothesis
labels.body: A testable interpretation or friction point that is not yet proven and must have a next verification action.

evidence.footer: Each material claim is recorded with its source, captured_at date, confidence, assumptions where applicable, and human approval status. Use “potential uncaptured opportunity” or “conversion friction,” never an unsourced claim that a company is losing a specific amount.

faq.heading: Questions foreign founders ask
faq.q1: Do I need a Japanese legal entity to start?
faq.a1: Not for every launch. The required structure depends on your offer, payment, fulfilment, support, tax, and regulated obligations. We coordinate implementation but do not replace legal or tax advice.
faq.q2: How do payments work without a Japanese bank?
faq.a2: After fit review, payment is arranged by Wise, bank transfer, USDC, or credit card through a Stripe invoice or payment link. The invoice confirms the recipient, fees, and (for USDC) the network and wallet; provider approval and fees remain separate.
faq.q3: How long until I'm live in Japan?
faq.a3: The Start Date is recorded after written scope acceptance, cleared payment, complete inputs, required access, and one empowered approver. If the agreed fixed setup is not delivered within 14 business days, 100% of the $12,000 setup fee is refunded; client-requested changes or holds pause the clock.
faq.q4: Do I need to speak or write Japanese?
faq.a4: No. Everything with you is in English. All Japanese-facing work — site, support, compliance — is handled on our side.
faq.a5: $12,000 one-time setup. The standard managed-operation fee is $2,000/month; the first 10 selected launch partners receive months 1–6 at $0/month. Month 7 onward is $2,000/month under the signed terms. Third-party costs and approved out-of-scope work are separate.
faq.q6: Can't I just use Google Translate or DeepL for my site?
faq.a6: Machine translation can help with words but does not decide information architecture, buyer context, required disclosures, provider constraints, trust signals, escalation, or ownership. The package addresses the agreed launch system, not translation alone.
faq.q7: How is Paradigm different from hiring my own Japanese team?
faq.a7: Hiring builds internal capability; the package is a fixed external launch scope. Choose based on control, timing, existing team capacity, and the responsibilities you need to retain internally.
faq.q8: What happens after the engagement ends? Will I be left on my own?
faq.a8: The agreed handover materials and ownership are documented in scope. The first 10 selected launch partners receive months 1–6 at $0/month, then managed operation is $2,000/month from month 7 onward under the signed terms; availability and scope are confirmed in writing.
